disclaimer: Static CLI-side characterization, corrected by coordinator body review. All 22 file hashes, exact 11-command cohort and 53 test declarations independently verified on Node24.19.0. No terminal command or original test in this cohort was executed. Empty errors arrays mean no additional handler-specific validation recorded, not absence of shared flag/selector/transport errors. Runtime-side behavior remains unproven.

rows.dispatch: client.call('terminal.list', {worktree, limit, includeVisualLayouts}) then annotateOmittedHostScope(client, result.result) before printing (terminal.ts:97-107)
errors: --limit must be a positive integer (flags.ts:77-88, getOptionalPositiveIntegerFlag)
rows.output: JSON: RPC envelope after in-place omittedHostSelectors annotation when hostScope lists omitted hosts; not byte-for-byte raw server data. printResult serializes that envelope. Text includes the scope, records, optional visual layout and truncation; an empty list returns early with only 'No terminals listed.' and scope (terminal-format.ts:21-40).
rows.hostScopeLiveness: annotateOmittedHostScope/resolveOmittedHostScopeSelectors (omitted-host-scope-selectors.ts:38-59) resolves ONLY whether an omitted host is selectable from this machine (local pairing store + SSH-target registry lookup) -- source comment verbatim: 'this answers can I select it, never is it up -- no host is claimed live or exited on this path.' formatListingHostScope (terminal-format.ts:24, omitted-host-scope-selectors.ts:99-116) renders 'scope: unverifiable' when the host reports no scope at all, distinct from an empty covered list.

defaults.terminal: active terminal in the resolved current worktree via getTerminalHandle -> client.call('terminal.resolveActive', {worktree}) when --terminal is omitted (selectors.ts:206-218)

rows.output: JSON: full RPC envelope, unmodified. Text: formatTerminalShow (terminal-format.ts:96-112) prints handle/title/worktree/branch/leaf/ptyId/connected/writable/agentWait/preview; agentWait is rendered 'unknown (not evaluated)' when undefined, distinct from 'none'.

errors: invalid_argument: '--cursor must be a non-negative integer' when --cursor is present but not /^\d+$/ (terminal.ts:116-123)

invalid_argument: '--screen reads the current rendered screen...' when both --screen and --cursor are present -- mutually exclusive by design, source comment: 'a screen read is the current frame and has nothing behind it to page' (terminal.ts:124-132)

incompatible_runtime: when --screen was requested but result.terminal.source is undefined -- an older host silently answered with accumulated output instead of a screen read; the CLI refuses to return that silently rather than let it be mistaken for the requested screen (terminal.ts:139-147)

Shared --limit requires a positive integer. --cursor first uses optional-string parsing (empty becomes omitted); digits-only then parseInt has no safe-integer/finite bound in this handler. --screen checks source absence only, not an enum; screen-unavailable is rendered with an accumulated-output warning.
rows.output: JSON: full RPC envelope, unmodified. Text: formatTerminalRead (terminal-format.ts:124-150) prints handle/status/source/draft/cursor/oldestCursor/latestCursor, a 'truncated' warning, a limited-output warning (two variants depending on which cursors differ), a 'screen-unavailable' warning, then a blank line and terminal.tail lines. `draft` is explicitly UI-only composer text per the spec's own note field -- never terminal output.

rows.dispatch: client.call('terminal.send', {terminal, text, enter, interrupt, agentPrompt?, client:{id:'orca-cli',type:'desktop'}})
rows.exitBehavior: process.exitCode=1 when !result.result.send.accepted (falsy, not strictly false), after printing the receipt; no throw in that branch.
rows.output: JSON: full RPC envelope, unmodified. Text: formatTerminalSend (terminal-format.ts:174-182) returns a structured refusal copy via structuredChatPtyWriteRefusalCopy(agentSessionRefusal, 'terminal-send') when result.send.agentSessionRefusal is set, else 'Sent <n> bytes to <handle>.'. `agentPrompt: true` is added to the RPC payload only when text && enter && !interrupt (terminal.ts:159) -- distinguishes a submitted agent prompt from a raw keystroke send.

rows.dispatch: client.call('terminal.wait', {terminal, for, timeoutMs}, {timeoutMs: <RPC transport timeout>}) -- note TWO distinct timeout concepts: the domain `timeoutMs` PARAM sent to the runtime (how long the WAIT CONDITION itself may take) vs the THIRD-ARGUMENT `timeoutMs` (the CLI<->runtime RPC transport's own timeout).
rows.rpcTimeoutDefault: Handler passes explicit transport timeout300000ms when domain timeout omitted, or requested positive timeoutMs+5000. Source comment mentions a historical generic15s cap, but inspected RuntimeClient constructor default is60000ms (runtime/client.ts:61-63). Do not treat that comment as the current generic default. Effective wire path beyond call(options) remains outside this slice.
errors: invalid_argument: 'Missing required --for' when --for is absent (flags.ts:5-11, getRequiredStringFlag) -- --for is NOT validated against the 'exit|tui-idle' enum client-side; the spec's usage string documents the values, but the handler forwards whatever string --for holds to the runtime unchecked.
Shared getOptionalPositiveIntegerFlag validates --timeout-ms as finite positive integer; getRequiredStringFlag rejects absent or empty --for, without validating the condition enum.
rows.exitBehavior: process.exitCode = 1 when result.result.wait.satisfied === false (terminal.ts:181-185) -- source comment: 'callers commonly chain terminal wait && terminal send; a structured blocked result is still an unsatisfied wait condition.'
rows.output: JSON: full RPC envelope, unmodified. Text: formatTerminalWait (terminal-format.ts:229-241) prints handle/condition/satisfied/status/exitCode ('null' literal when absent), plus blockedReason when present.
testFiles: src/cli/index-terminal-commands.test.ts (it: 'exits nonzero when terminal wait returns an unsatisfied blocked result')

rows.dispatch: client.call('terminal.stop', {worktree}) -- worktree resolved via getRequiredWorktreeSelector, which DOES accept 'active'/'current' and resolves them via cwd (selectors.ts:159-171), but the --worktree flag itself is mandatory (no cwd auto-default when omitted entirely).
rows.deprecation: Hidden compatibility spec recommends terminal close --worktree <selector> --all. This CLI handler still calls terminal.stop and formats its stopped count, without the CLI close handlers' verdict checks. Tab/layout/resume effects in terminal.stop's runtime implementation are untraced, not asserted absent.
rows.output: JSON: full RPC envelope, unmodified. Text: inline formatter '`Stopped ${value.stopped} terminals.`' (terminal.ts:191) -- no dedicated terminal-format.ts function.
rows.destructiveRegistryNote: The spec lacks a destructive property; census normalizes that absence to false. It is NOT a claim that stopping processes is nondestructive or authorized in an audit.

defaults.title: null when --title is omitted OR passed as an empty string -- getOptionalStringFlag treats '' the same as absent (flags.ts:24-30), so title:null is sent either way, which the RUNTIME (not the CLI) interprets as 'reset to the auto-generated title' per the spec's own note.

rows.output: JSON: full RPC envelope, unmodified. Text: formatTerminalRename (terminal-format.ts:184-188) -- 'Renamed terminal <handle> to "<title>".' when result.rename.title is truthy, else 'Cleared title for terminal <handle>.'

defaults.worktree: Guard first rejects remote client when flags.has('worktree') is false. Otherwise getBrowserWorktreeSelector resolves the value: 'all' or empty-string can yield undefined, including on remote; explicit active/current reject on remote; omitted local resolves cwd with catch-all fallback to undefined. No unconditional remote-omitted success path.

rows.dispatch: client.call('terminal.create', {worktree,command,title,focus,...(focus?{presentation:'focused'}:{}),...(useRendererBackedInteractiveTerminal?{rendererBacked:true,activate:focus}:{})}). presentation depends only on focus, including remote; rendererBacked/activate depend separately on the local interactive classifier.
rows.localVsRemoteDispatch: !client.isRemote && shouldUseRendererBackedInteractiveTerminal(command) decides whether to add rendererBacked:true+activate:focus (terminal.ts:208-209,220) -- this decision is NEVER made for a remote client (client.isRemote short-circuits it to false), regardless of the command string.
rows.commandClassification: shouldUseRendererBackedInteractiveTerminal (codex-command-classification.ts:288-307): tokenizes --command (max 32 leading shell words), strips a shell-launch prefix, takes the executable basename; if it's a Codex executable, returns true unless the tokens form a non-interactive Codex subcommand; if it's a Claude executable, returns true unless a later token is a help/version/print flag; otherwise false. Deeper tokenization/classification helper bodies (isCodexExecutable, isNonInteractiveCodexSubcommand, isClaudeExecutable, isClaudePrintFlag, stripShellLaunchPrefix) are named but not individually traced in this document -- bounded, untraced runtime behavior.
errors: invalid_argument: 'Remote terminal create requires --worktree...' when client.isRemote && !flags.has('worktree') (terminal.ts:201-206)
rows.output: JSON: full RPC envelope, unmodified. Text: formatTerminalCreate (terminal-format.ts:190-195) -- 'Created terminal <handle>' plus optional title/surface/warning suffixes.
testFiles: src/cli/index-terminal-commands.test.ts (multiple: focus-through-create, Codex/Claude backgrounding, remote worktree requirement)

rows.aliasNote: 'terminal focus' resolves to canonical 'terminal switch' via CommandSpec.aliases BEFORE dispatch (source comment at terminal.ts:224 confirms this verbatim); TERMINAL_HANDLERS has exactly one entry ('terminal switch') for both surface names -- there is no separate 'terminal focus' handler key.
rows.output: JSON: full RPC envelope, unmodified. Text: formatTerminalFocus (terminal-format.ts:201-206) -- 'Focused terminal <handle> (tab <tabId>).' or, when result.focus.navigated===false, 'Focus request for terminal <handle> was superseded or host navigation was skipped (tab <tabId>).'

defaults.terminal: active terminal via getTerminalHandle, ONLY reached in the non---all branch

rows.dispatch: Three possible RPC method names in two branches: --all => terminal.closeAll({worktree:required}); otherwise --tab => terminal.closeTab({terminal}), else terminal.close({terminal}).
errors: invalid_argument: '--all uses --worktree and cannot be combined with --terminal or --tab' when --all is set together with --terminal or --tab (terminal.ts:227-233)
invalid_argument: 'Closing a workspace requires --all: terminal close --worktree <selector> --all' when --worktree is given WITHOUT --all (terminal.ts:261-266)

incompatible_runtime: 'This Orca host does not support closing every terminal in a workspace yet...' when the --all RPC call itself fails with method_not_found (terminal.ts:251-258) -- re-thrown as a clearer error, not swallowed.
rows.livenessVerdictHandling: Single close: no CLI failure when ptyKilled truthy OR ptyStopVerdict===undefined; otherwise live -> terminal_stop_live, any other supplied value -> terminal_stop_unverifiable. Bulk close: no CLI failure when !ptyStopVerdict; otherwise live -> terminal_stop_live, other truthy verdict -> terminal_stop_unverifiable. The bulk helper has NO ptyKilled shortcut. Missing legacy verdict yields a non-failing CLI receipt, not positive evidence of death.
rows.exitBehavior: Failure sets exitCode=1. Bulk always calls reportCliError(failure,json), hence text goes to stderr as an error; single close uses reportCliError only for JSON and prints formatTerminalClose for text. Tab-mode text returns 'Closed terminal tab...' before the PTY suffix helper, so do not promise a warning suffix there.
rows.output: JSON success envelope is printed; classified failures become local error envelope retaining close receipt in error.data. Bulk success text gives closed/stopped counts. Single formatTerminalClose returns tab-only text when closeMode==='tab'; otherwise confirmed ptyKilled adds 'PTY killed.', literal live/unverifiable add their warnings, undefined/other values add no suffix. CLI success without a verdict is not verified death.
testFiles: src/cli/handlers/terminal.test.ts (describe: 'terminal close CLI', incl. it.each 'rejects ambiguous bulk-close flags' [3 cases], 'fails safely before mutation when the host predates bulk close')

errors: invalid_argument: '--direction must be horizontal or vertical' when --direction is present and matches neither literal exactly (terminal.ts:288-295) -- client-side enum validation, unlike terminal wait's --for.
rows.output: JSON: full RPC envelope, unmodified. Text: formatTerminalSplit (terminal-format.ts:197-199) -- 'Split pane <handle> in tab <tabId>'.

sharedHelperContracts.getTerminalHandle (src/cli/selectors.ts:: Used by show/read/send/wait/rename/switch/split/close(non---all). Returns the EXPLICIT --terminal value verbatim if present; otherwise resolves the worktree via getBrowserWorktreeSelector and calls client.call('terminal.resolveActive', {worktree}) to get the active terminal's handle for that worktree. This is the single default-resolution path shared by 8 of the 11 commands.
sharedHelperContracts.getBrowserWorktreeSelector (src/cli/sele: Directly used by create and indirectly by8 handle-resolving commands. all -> undefined; active/current require local client and resolve enclosing worktree; other explicit selectors pass through caller-WSL normalization. Omitted remote -> undefined. Omitted local attempts cwd resolution but catches EVERY error (including failed worktree.list), not only selector_not_found. That fallback behavior is source parity, not evidence of healthy host.
sharedHelperContracts.getRequiredWorktreeSelector / getOptiona: Required by stop and close --all, optional by list. active/current require local and resolve cwd; other values normalize. Omitted required throws Missing required --worktree; omitted optional returns undefined. These helpers do not special-case 'all' like getBrowserWorktreeSelector.
sharedHelperContracts.client.call(method, params, opts?) (src/: isRemote getter (client.ts:83-85) is true iff a remote pairing was resolved from userDataPath/pairingCode/environmentSelector at client construction; this is the ONLY local-vs-remote branch point visible at the terminal-handler layer (client.isRemote checked directly in terminal.ts for terminal create, and indirectly via the selector helpers above). When isRemote, call() routes through a lazily-loaded WebSocket transport (client.ts:118-124); the local (non-remote) dispatch path, full SSH host-resolution mechanics, and the generic RPC transport timeout/retry machinery are NOT traced further in this document -- named as bounded, untraced runtime infrastructure shared across all CLI domains, not specific to terminal commands.
sharedHelperContracts.printResult / prepareComputerCliJsonResu: JSON serializes prepareComputerCliJsonResult(response). Its early return preserves responses without result.screenshotStatus. Terminal list has already annotated omittedHostSelectors in place. Close failure bypasses success printing. Therefore this is envelope-shaped JSON, not a universal raw-server-verbatim guarantee.
Bulk liveness failure always uses reportCliError: JSON envelope or text stderr. Single close failure uses this for JSON only and formatTerminalClose for text. Both set nonzero exitCode. reportCliError itself does not run the single-close text formatter.

genuineUnknowns: Full local (non-remote) RPC dispatch path inside client.call and the SSH host-resolution/ownership mechanics beyond what selectors/omitted-host-scope-selectors expose are shared, cross-domain runtime infrastructure -- not traced in this terminal-only slice.

codex-command-classification.ts's deeper helpers (isCodexExecutable, isNonInteractiveCodexSubcommand, isClaudeExecutable, isClaudePrintFlag, tokenizeLeadingShellWords, stripShellLaunchPrefix) were named at their call site but their own bodies were not individually read -- shouldUseRendererBackedInteractiveTerminal's OWN body (lines 288-307) was read in full.

The runtime-side (main process / native host) implementations of terminal.list/show/read/send/wait/stop/create/focus/close/closeTab/closeAll/split/resolveActive are outside src/cli and outside this document's scope entirely -- only the CLI-side request shape and CLI-side response handling are characterized.
livenessAndHostOwnershipInvariant: Process verdict vocabulary remains live/unverifiable/exited. These close receipt handlers use failure hints live/unverifiable, not a full liveness classifier; missing verdict can pass for older hosts without confirming death. Single and bulk guards differ. Formatter emits a killed suffix only for truthy ptyKilled outside tab mode; it warns only for literal live/unverifiable. Remote contact loss must not be promoted to exited.
